name: Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA)
intendedUse: The README says DVWA is deliberately vulnerable, for practising security testing and teaching in a legal setting, never Internet-facing: https://github.com/digininja/DVWA/blob/a96943dc1f52f390ee5df72144660636c4b7dd06/README.md

image.note: GHCR has no '2.5' tag; images are tagged by short commit SHA, and a96943d is exactly the 2.5 commit (single-platform Docker v2 manifest, not an index). compose.yml at the tag uses :latest (currently sha256:8029450682bd70e2e8cd1ffe8e46dd1885ff2a913296091cebfa8ba0a7d36498, a later build, not used). DB service per compose.yml: docker.io/library/mariadb:10 @ sha256:0d0945c57f75b3a3b9ebe71aedaaad005fa5305054e8fca3d2e42a8c92b43b5e (index digest of the moving tag, resolved 2026-10-22; set DB_SERVER=db). Runner steps: log in at /login.php with admin/password, create the DB via /setup.php (Create / Reset Database), then set security level to low (the tag defaults to impossible; DEFAULT_SECURITY_LEVEL=low or /security.php). All /vulnerabilities/<module>/ pages need the logged-in session.

answerKey.title: DVWA vulnerability modules (vulnerabilities/<module>/source and help pages)

builtBy: Claude (AI-assisted), from the DVWA 2.5 module list, help pages, low.php sources and README; to be checked by labeller A

vulnerabilities.title: Brute Force
vulnerabilities.description: Login form has no attempt limiting or lockout, so passwords can be guessed repeatedly.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. GET form with username/password params; the page itself sits behind the DVWA session. Low also concatenates username into SQL (not documented, not listed).

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection
vulnerabilities.description: IP address field is passed to a ping shell command, allowing extra OS commands.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. POST param ip.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection (source sink)
vulnerabilities.description: Request input concatenated straight into shell_exec ping command.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. PHP: Penthera's route analysis reads JS/TS only.

vulnerabilities.title: CSRF
vulnerabilities.description: Password change via GET without any anti-CSRF token or re-authentication.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored.

vulnerabilities.title: File Inclusion
vulnerabilities.description: page parameter is included directly, allowing local and remote file inclusion.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. LFI/path traversal not claimed; RFI would also need an external server (allow_url_include is on in the shipped php.ini).

vulnerabilities.title: File Upload
vulnerabilities.description: Uploads are stored in a web-served folder without any type or content checks.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure CAPTCHA
vulnerabilities.description: Second step of the password change trusts a client-supplied step value, skipping the CAPTCHA.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. Needs reCAPTCHA keys configured; the default config has none.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection
vulnerabilities.description: User id parameter is concatenated into a SQL query; database errors are shown.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. GET param id (with Submit). SQL string building in source is not a code-sink entry per spec.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection (Blind)
vulnerabilities.description: User id is concatenated into SQL; only exists/missing (200/404) differs, so boolean or time based.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. GET param id (with Submit); errors suppressed.

vulnerabilities.title: Weak Session IDs
vulnerabilities.description: dvwaSession cookie value is a simple incrementing counter, so it is predictable.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. Predictable token is weak-crypto/session class. The cookie also lacks HttpOnly/Secure at low, but that is not the documented item.

vulnerabilities.title: XSS (DOM)
vulnerabilities.description: Page script writes the default URL parameter into the document without encoding.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored.

vulnerabilities.title: XSS (Reflected)
vulnerabilities.description: name parameter is echoed into the HTML response unencoded; X-XSS-Protection disabled.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. GET param name. No repo entry: the sink is a PHP string echo, not a JS innerHTML sink.

vulnerabilities.title: XSS (Stored)
vulnerabilities.description: Guestbook name and message are stored and rendered later without HTML encoding.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored.

vulnerabilities.title: CSP Bypass
vulnerabilities.description: Content-Security-Policy script-src allows third-party hosts where attackers can host scripts.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. Over-permissive CSP header only on this page. Exploiting it (POST include param) needs a browser; the permissive header itself is the scored item.

vulnerabilities.title: JavaScript
vulnerabilities.description: Security token is computed client-side in page JavaScript, so it can be forged.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored.

vulnerabilities.title: Authorisation Bypass
vulnerabilities.description: Admin-only page is hidden from the menu but not access-checked for other users.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. Needs a second, non-admin account (e.g. gordonb) to observe.

vulnerabilities.title: Open HTTP Redirect
vulnerabilities.description: redirect parameter is placed in the Location header without any validation.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. The redirect script is linked from the authenticated module page but does not itself check the session; it answers 500 without the param.

vulnerabilities.title: Cryptography
vulnerabilities.description: Messages are XOR-encoded with a fixed key and Base64, which is reversible encoding, not encryption.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. The XOR key is hardcoded in low.php, but it is the exercise's cipher key, not a credential/API/signing secret.

vulnerabilities.title: API
vulnerabilities.description: Older v1 user endpoint is still live and returns password hashes that v2 hides.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. Excess fields in a versioned API response need app knowledge to judge; not a served file/spec/debug endpoint. API router has no DVWA session check. Needs composer vendor/, which the Dockerfile does not install, so it may not work in the image.

vulnerabilities.title: Default credentials
vulnerabilities.description: Application ships with documented default login admin / password.
vulnerabilities.note: Low level only; medium/high not scored. The runner uses these to log in; other seeded users have weak passwords too.

vulnerabilities.title: Default database password in config template
vulnerabilities.description: Config template falls back to a documented default database password when no environment variable is set.
vulnerabilities.note: Documented default in a .dist template (Dockerfile copies it to config.inc.php); compose.yml sets the same DB password plus a root password. Not a leaked secret, so not scored as secrets; a secrets finding here is a documented default, not a false positive.
